correctness.rationale: The domain is connected noncomplete complete multipartite graphs on fixed N>=3. Every selected pair in different parts is adjacent; two selected vertices in one part are geodesically visible exactly if an omitted vertex lies outside their part. For complement T of t>=1 vertices, the mutually disjoint bad events are T contained in some part of size >=t+2; hence r_{N-t}=C(N,t)-sum_{n_i>=t+2}C(n_i,t), and r_N=0. Parts at most 2 make every proper set visible, and a part >=3 produces a nonvisible proper set. For r_3, only the star has any bad triple and r_3(star)=C(N-1,3); for r_{N-1}, the exact formula is sum_{n_i<=2}n_i. At N>=6, K_{3,N-3} has near-top coefficient 0, below the star's 1, so no minimum; N=3,4,5 are checked by the remaining nontrivial coefficients. Independent elementary partition enumeration for N=3..13 reproduced maximum and threshold; actual verifier checks direct geodesics through N=10, partition enumeration through N=30; these computations corroborate the all-N proof, not replace it.
